title: Upholstery, metals, glass and stone
intro: Complementary materials serve different roles. Separate upholstery, cushioning, surfaces and supports, then review the actual products, their interfaces and maintenance requirements.

sections.title: Separate cover, cushioning and support
sections.text: In an upholstered seat, specify cover, liner, filling, support and frame separately. Request fabric identification, intended use and cleaning instructions, filling data and a seating sample. A fabric colour or one foam property is not a complete comfort specification. Review the assembly and whether covers can be maintained or replaced.
sections.caption: Each layer has a role; assess the assembly together.

sections.title: Review interfaces between different materials
sections.text: For glass or stone on a metal base, identify the product, dimensions, support and connection system. Request edge, protection and joint details for the selected assembly. Do not infer thickness or capacity from a photograph. Obtain supplier data and technical review, including installation access and possible disassembly.
sections.caption: The material interface needs a reviewed connection detail.

sections.title: Document use, care and maintenance
sections.text: Link each surface to its use environment and declared care method, considering liquids, abrasion and light exposure. Record product limits instead of a general durability claim. Review samples according to supplier instructions and identify replaceable parts. Deliver material codes and care information so maintenance does not depend on guesswork.
sections.caption: Care records belong to identified products.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: A client selects a chair from an appealing photograph. Filling, support and removable-cover details are unknown. Daily use and frequent cleaning require evidence beyond the image.
example.decision: Decision: request layer specifications, care information and a seating sample before approving the upholstery system.

quiz.question: Does changing fabric establish chair comfort?
options: No; filling, support, frame and user also need review
quiz.explanation: The cover is one component; it does not prove the whole seat fits the user.

assignment.prompt: Create a seat-layer schedule and an interface information sheet for a surface on a different-material base.
criteria: Capacity is not inferred from appearance

faq.question: Should I test an arbitrary cleaner on the sample?
faq.answer: Follow the product’s permitted care and test instructions; do not generalise one sample result to other surface systems.
